bites.title: A dimmer, not a light switch
bites.body:
Your pen isn't on or off. It's a dimmer switch. I've picked a brush where pressure changes size AND darkness, so you can see every ounce.

Every test here is graded against your own feather and lean from lesson 00. Skipped it? I'll use a generic range.

bites.title: Crescendo
bites.body:
One stroke, at least 4 cm. Start feather light and press harder the whole way, ending heavy.

On the seismograph, the ember should climb like a ramp.

bites.title: Thin, THICK, thin
bites.body: The ink line every comic inker dreams about. Land soft, swell in the middle, lift off soft. Think of a plane touching down and taking off again.
bites.hint: Keep moving while you lift. Stopping and then lifting leaves a blob.

bites.title: Hold it steady
bites.body: Now the hardest one: the same pressure for the whole stroke, at least 6 cm. The ember should be a flat plateau.

bites.title: Slow is control
bites.body: Draw a slow, careful stroke, under 50 mm per second. Like tracing a contour you really care about.

bites.title: Fast is straight
bites.body: Now flick! Over 200 mm per second. Fast strokes come out straighter and more confident than slow ones. Commit.

bites.title: 04 cleared
bites.body: Crescendo, swell, plateau, slow, fast. Your hand knows five new things. These all live in the Dojo as drills with scores and streaks. Warm up with two minutes of them every session.
